method.canonical: isolated tmux server; pane shell disabled echo, read one newline-terminated line, printed it between OUT markers; tmux send-keys -l supplied payload and a separate named Enter submitted it
method.raw: isolated tmux server; pane ran stty raw -echo and dd count=<payload bytes>; compared tmux send-keys -l with load-buffer from stdin plus paste-buffer

decision: Use a uniquely named tmux buffer loaded through stdin, paste it into the target pane, delete it as part of paste-buffer, then submit a separate named Enter.
rationale: The live probe confirms a hard 1023-byte canonical-line boundary while a raw TUI consumes 3028 bytes intact. load-buffer avoids placing the full framed body in the tmux send-keys argv and uses tmux's native paste path; the separate Enter preserves the existing no-smuggled-submit invariant. The implementation still requires a real 3000+ byte adapter regression and live OMP witness.
